Reasoning

• Classical Electrodynamics (B):  Even without quantisation it is plagued by the infinite self-energy of a point charge.  One routinely has to introduce an ad-hoc short–distance cutoff (a finite “classical electron radius”) to make the field energy finite.  Hence a UV regularisation is needed.

• Quantum Electrodynamics (C):  Loop integrals diverge in the ultraviolet.  One introduces a regulator (cut-off, dimensional regularisation, Pauli–Villars, …) and then renormalises.  So QED certainly needs UV regularisation.

• Quantum Chromodynamics (A):  Although QCD is asymptotically free, its loop diagrams are still ultraviolet divergent; the theory is made sensible only after the usual machinery of regularisation and renormalisation.  Asymptotic freedom means the renormalised coupling goes to zero at high energies, not that no regularisation is required.

• Superstring Theory (D):  Because the fundamental objects are one-dimensional strings, interactions are smeared over a finite length (the string length).  The extended nature of the string together with world-sheet modular invariance removes the short-distance (high-energy) divergences that plague point-particle theories.  Perturbative superstring amplitudes are ultraviolet finite at every order; no separate UV regulator is needed.

Hence, the only option that “never requires regularisation at high energies” is superstring theory.

Answer: D
